recentKeyChanges.title: Tesla robotaxi expands to Miami and Dallas on July 3
recentKeyChanges.description: On July 3, 2026, Tesla expanded its unsupervised robotaxi service to Miami and Dallas, marking continued geographic expansion of the Cybercab platform. City officials report Tesla's Austin fleet at approximately 50 vehicles despite a year of operation. Production is ramping exponentially toward year-end per Musk, but software limitations rather than vehicle manufacturing capacity remain the primary constraint on service scaling.

recentKeyChanges.title: Tesla app adds live Self-Driving indicator for robotaxi owners
recentKeyChanges.description: Tesla app version 4.58.5 (reported July 7, 2026) displays a live blue 'Self-Driving' indicator under the speed readout when FSD is engaged, plus the glowing blue navigation path. Confirmed working on HW3 Model S. Vehicle-side software 2026.20.6.1 has reached ~40% of the fleet. For owners whose vehicles generate robotaxi revenue, this turns the app into a basic fleet monitor — especially relevant as unsupervised service runs in Miami and other cities.

recentKeyChanges.title: Tesla announces Cybercab 'employee rides' at Giga Texas - parking lot only
recentKeyChanges.description: On July 10, 2026, Tesla's Robotaxi account posted a video of a gold Cybercab driving across the Giga Texas outbound lot, with Tesla's main account quote-tweeting: 'Cybercab employee rides at Giga Texas starting soon.' However, the announcement is deliberately vague - Tesla gave no details on route, fleet size, or whether rides occur on public roads versus private factory property. Electrek reported on July 11 that the announcement appears to be nothing more than parking-lot ferries for employees, noting 'for any other automaker, our car drove an employee across the parking lot would not be a news event.' The announcement generated 2.9 million views but no substantive progress toward commercial deployment.

positive_signals: Video shows Cybercab driving autonomously at Giga Texas
Vehicle operates without steering wheel or pedals
Engineering lead reported 50 rides in recent days
negative_signals: No route details provided - appears limited to parking lot
No confirmation of public road operations
Electrek calls it a non-event: just parking lot shuttle
Announcement vague and insubstantive compared to competitors
Does not address fundamental scaling issues

latestMetric.note: Estimated 120+ Cybercabs visible at Giga Texas staging lots per drone footage and social media reports. Production ramping since February 2026 start, but vehicles remain in staging - not deployed commercially due to lack of regulatory approval for autonomous operation.
